title: The subjunctive after requests: asking the king to act

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the subjunctive after advice and requests (*aconsejar que*, *recomendar que*) from B1 Unit 4. *Pedir que*, *querer que* and *ordenar que* work the same way: they are followed by the subjunctive when the two verbs have different subjects. Texts about Las Casas often use the present for past events, so the subjunctive is in the present too.

sections.title: Request + que + subjunctive
rows: Las Casas pide al rey que proteja a los indígenas.
Los colonos quieren que el rey cambie las leyes.
Las Casas quiere ayudar a los indígenas.
One subject: use the infinitive, no *que*.

items.spanish: Las Casas pide al rey que proteja a los indígenas.
items.english: Las Casas asks the king to protect the indigenous people.

items.spanish: Los colonos quieren que el rey cambie las leyes.
items.english: The settlers want the king to change the laws.

items.spanish: El rey ordena que se reúna una junta en Valladolid.
items.english: The king orders a council to meet in Valladolid.

items.spanish: Las Casas pide que se prohíban los abusos.
items.english: Las Casas asks for the abuses to be forbidden.

sections.content: The subjunctive swaps the vowel: *-ar* verbs take *-e* (*cambiar → cambie*), *-er* and *-ir* verbs take *-a* (*proteger → proteja*). Use *que* + subjunctive only when the person who asks and the person who acts are different.
